items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: three ACs: own commit before the release commit, other staged work and in-flight runs untouched, the release never stops; each has tests on real git repos

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: every failure maps to a status and exit 0; a failure after the fold started rolls the tree back (archive removed, drops restored, index reset); hooks never bypassed; commit timeout and git errors are handled

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: no shell string building: git arguments are lists, paths go on stdin NUL-separated; no credentials; nothing outside the project root is touched

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: 19 tests: own commit, staged and unstaged work kept, untracked drop of another run, idempotence, legacy layout, conflict, no trunk, trunk from origin/HEAD, undeletable file, half-deleted fold, refusing hook (tree compared before and after), local changes, 900 files

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: one plan, one add, one commit; the dirty check lists the drops folder once

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: new tool next to fold_events.py and reuses its stage helpers (_stage now returns the staged paths); ruff clean

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: producer: fold tool JSON status; consumer: changelog skill Step 5.3 reads status and open_files; the F11 events integrity check already accepts a fold commit; the skill's step order (before 5.5) and the autonomous shortcut sentence were fixed
